To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the M. tuberculosis TetR family regulators, Rv3249 and Rv1817, are capable of binding palmitic acid, a fatty acid, and that this binding event is critical for the repression of the mmpL genes, which encode a family of lipid transporters.

the structures of the TetR family proteins Rv3249 and Rv1818 reveal that they are dimeric, with each domain of the dimer containing a fatty acid molecule, and that these proteins are able to recognize promoter and intragenics regions of the MmpLS.

the crystal structures of Rv3240c and Rv1826, two regulators of MmpL transporters, reveal the presence of bound ligands, palmitic acid and isopropyle laurate, respectively, which suggests that fatty acids and fatty acid esters may be natural ligand of these regulators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional analysis of the MmpS/MmpL family of membrane proteins.
understanding how the M. tuberculosis cell wall is assembled and maintained, and how it is regulated by transcription factors and small molecules.
the regulation of the Mycobacterial membrane protein L family of transporters, which are essential for cell wall biosynthesis and virulence of these organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MmpS/MmpL transporters are important for the virulence of mycobacteria, and that their regulation is controlled by the TetR family regulatory proteins Rv3249 and Rv1815.
the crystal structures of the Rv1816 and Rv3249 transcriptional regulators reveal the presence of fatty acid ligands, which may serve as the natural ligands for the regulators.
the crystal structures of the two M. tuberculosis TetR family regulators, Rv3249 and Rv1818, have been solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
saturated fatty acids are natural ligands for Rv3249 and Rv1818 and that the expression of Mmp L genes are controlled by fatty acids.
the MmpLS are regulated by the TetR family proteins Rv1816 and Rv3249.
the expression of MmpLS is controlled by a two-component regulatory system, Rv3249/3249c, and a TetR-family regulator, Rv1816; and palmitic acid is a natural ligand for these two regulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MmpS-MmpL system is regulated by a complex network of regulators that includes TetR family proteins.
fatty acids may serve as ligands for these regulatory proteins.
fatty acids may function as natural ligands for Rv3249 and Rv1815.
